name.text: Equation of a wave from its graph

questiontext.text:
The graph shows a wave of the form \(y = a\sin bx\) or \(y = a\cos bx\) for \(0^\circ \le x \le {@xmax@}^\circ\).

[[jsxgraph width="520px" height="300px"]] (function() { // static board: grid, axes and one wave; x in degrees var xl = 0, xr = {#xmax#}, yl = {#ylo#}, yu = {#yhi#}; var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [xl - (xr-xl)*0.04, yu, xr + (xr-xl)*0.02, yl], axis: false, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}}); var g = {strokeColor: '#dddddd', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}; for (var gx = Math.ceil(xl/({#xg#}))*({#xg#}); gx <= xr + 1e-9; gx += {#xg#}) { b.create('segment', [[gx, yl], [gx, yu]], g); } for (var gy = Math.ceil(yl/(0.5))*(0.5); gy <= yu + 1e-9; gy += 0.5) { b.create('segment', [[xl, gy], [xr, gy]], g); } var ax = {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}; b.create('segment', [[xl, 0], [xr, 0]], ax); b.create('segment', [[0, yl], [0, yu]], ax); var t = {fixed: true, highlight: false, useMathJax: false, fontSize: 11, anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'top'}; for (var tx = Math.ceil(xl/({#xt#}))*({#xt#}); tx <= xr + 1e-9; tx += {#xt#}) { if (Math.abs(tx) > 1e-9) { b.create('text', [tx, -(yu-yl)*0.015, String(Math.round(tx*10)/10) + '\u00b0'], t); } } var ty = {fixed: true, highlight: false, useMathJax: false, fontSize: 11, anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'middle'}; for (var tv = Math.ceil(yl/(1))*(1); tv <= yu + 1e-9; tv += 1) { if (Math.abs(tv) > 1e-9) { b.create('text', [-(xr-xl)*0.01, tv, String(Math.round(tv*10)/10)], ty); } } b.create('functiongraph', [function(x) { return ({#a#})*({#fs#}==1 ? Math.sin(Math.PI*({#b#})*x/180) : Math.cos(Math.PI*({#b#})*x/180)); }, xl, xr], {strokeColor: '#1f4e9c', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

Write an equation for the wave.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The greatest value is \({@a@}\) and the least is \({@-a@}\), so the amplitude is \({@a@}\).

One complete wave is \({@per@}^\circ\) long, so \(b = 360^\circ \div {@per@}^\circ = {@b@}\).

At \(x = 0\) the graph is at \({@y0@}\), so it is a {@fword@}: \(y = {@ta@}\).

Other equations describe the same wave, for example \(y = {@talt@}\) (angle in degrees).

questiondescription.text:
Trigonometry III: equation of a wave from its graph

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.5: Write an equation y = a sin bx or y = a cos bx for a wave drawn in degrees; any equivalent equation is accepted.

Core

This question is adapted from Question 1 in Exercise B of Chapter 7 of Cassell, D., Instone, S., Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP AS/A2 Mathematics: Core 2 for AQA, Cambridge University Press, 2004: a drawn graph with two stretches instead of a sketch, randomised over a curated list, any equivalent equation accepted and named feedback added.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: Your wave has period \({@360*b@}^\circ\), but one complete wave on the graph is \({@per@}^\circ\) long. Check the number multiplying \(x\): the period is \(360^\circ\) divided by it.
Your wave is twice as tall. The amplitude is half of (greatest \(-\) least).
Right height and period, but at \(x = 0\) the graph is at \({@y0@}\), and your equation gives a different value. Use {@fword@}.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="ownok"]]

Test your equation against the graph. At \(x = 0^\circ\) the graph is at \({@nice(y0)@}\) and your equation gives \({@nice(own0)@}\). At \(x = {@nice(xq)@}^\circ\) the graph is at \({@nice(gq)@}\) and your equation gives \({@nice(ownq)@}\).

[[/if]]

Read the amplitude from the greatest and least values and the period from one complete wave; the number multiplying \(x\) is \(360^\circ \div\) period.

qtest.description: Correct: written the other way round
Invalid: an expression with a stray y
